title: Receiver Behavior checks account-level receiptSharing, not effective preference
description:
Location: draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md, Peer/receipt / Receiver Behavior, line ~315.

The Sender Behavior (line ~306) correctly computes the effective receipt-sharing preference: 'if Chat.receiptSharing is present for the relevant Chat, that value is used; otherwise the account-level PresenceStatus.receiptSharing applies.' This is the correct two-level override logic.

The Receiver Behavior, however, reads: 'when the receiving account has PresenceStatus.receiptSharing set to false' — it checks only the account-level field and ignores Chat.receiptSharing entirely.

This creates an asymmetry: a per-chat receiptSharing=false override suppresses outbound Peer/receipt calls (via Sender Behavior), but does NOT suppress inbound Peer/receipt delivery on the receiving side. The two behaviors are inconsistent and will produce incorrect results when Chat.receiptSharing=false while PresenceStatus.receiptSharing=true.

Correct behavior: The Receiver Behavior MUST compute the effective preference using the same two-level logic as the Sender Behavior (Chat.receiptSharing if present, else PresenceStatus.receiptSharing), and apply the suppression when the effective preference is false.
close_reason: Fixed: Receiver Behavior now uses effective preference same as Sender Behavior (federation-00.md:315)
